company.name: Gen1E Lifesciences
company.shortDescription: GEn1E is a clinical-stage multi-target AI platform. They develop novel, next-gen, immunomodulators for rare & inflammatory diseases.
company.description:
GEn1E Lifesciences is a Clinical-stage, multi-target company with a unique AI platform. They develop novel, next-generation, immunomodulatory therapies for rare & inflammatory diseases with no effective treatments. GEn1E is supercharging the drug development cycle by applying AI to multiple-mechanism-of-action protein targets and their natural platform capabilities—creating novel therapeutics at an unprecedented pace. Their AI platform has enabled them to develop a purpose-built therapy for ARDS to reduce its $20 billion cost on society (just in the USA). 
 
GEn1E has built a rich pipeline of 21+ novel and selective immunomodulators and has plans to accelerate 2 additional devastating diseases (beyond their lead indication) to IND in the next 12 months. Their AI platform enables tremendous pace and capital efficiency as demonstrated by their progress in ~2 years with seed capital—a stark contrast to the typical spend of $100M+ and 7+ years exhibited in the pharmaceuticals / biotech industry.
 
With ~90% of rare diseases having no therapeutic treatment at all, GEn1E is taking a giant swing that will hopefully bring life-saving therapies to the lives of patients in need.
 
GEn1E’s team has decades of experience in drug development and machine learning, and they graduated from YCombinator and Stanford-StartX in late 2019. GEn1E is based in Palo Alto, CA.

aiResearchSummary.text: Gen1E Lifesciences is engaged in developing substituted naphthyl p38alpha mitogen-activated protein kinase inhibitors and related pharmaceutical compositions for disease treatment, as described in 'Substituted naphthyl p38alpha mitogen-activated protein kinase inhibitors.' The company is also advancing machine learning methods and systems for sub-phenotyping acute respiratory distress syndrome patients, as detailed in 'Machine learning methods and systems for acute respiratory distress syndrome.' These efforts target immunomodulation and rare or inflammatory diseases.
